messages:
maya: Heads-up — after the scheduler tweak this morning I'm seeing a weird drop in prefix-cache hit-rate on the 8x GPU pool. Not a huge tail latency spike but hit-rate fell from ~72% -> ~41% for short prompts.

josh: ugh. which tweak exactly? the continuous-batching window change?

maya: yeah, we raised the batch_window from 8ms -> 18ms to improve throughput for long convo traffic. Rollout id: rollout/continuous-batcher-v3.

li: quick note — kernel selector also started preferring the new fused-attn kernel for seq_len <= 64 in that same deploy. Could be grouping/packing effects.

maya: here's the short profiler dump around a sample minute (from /svc/runtime/metrics):
```
minute=2026-11-03T10:23Z
requests=12k
avg_seq=32
prefix_cache_hits=4920 (41.0%)
prefix_cache_lookups=12000
avg_p95_latency_ms=42
queueing_time_ms_p95=9
batch_size_p50=6
batch_size_p95=18
```

maya: baseline before rollback: prefix_cache_hits=8640 (72.0%) with batch_window=8ms and kernel=fused-attn-v2; p95 latency ~38ms

josh: interesting — batch_size_p95 went up after window increase? that should raise hit-rate normally. maybe batch composition changed so prefixes are mixed across cohorts.

li: hypothesis: the longer window increased chance of unrelated requests being coalesced. Continuous batching started pulling cold prefixes into batches with warm prefixes and evicting earlier cache entries due to KV churn. Also the fused-attn kernel grouping may change memory layout causing different prefetch timing.

maya: I ran a small repro targeting the 8x pool — steps:
1) spawn 2 traffic cohorts: short-prefixed prompts (repeated prefix hash A) at 200qps and infrequent random prompts at 50qps.
2) toggle batch_window and kernel flag.
3) collect prefix hits per cohort.

repro command:
```
./tools/bench --pool 8x --cohort-a=200qps --cohort-b=50qps --prefix=A --duration=300s --trace-prefix-hits /tmp/pfx.csv
```

josh: can you share traces? I'll correlate with eviction counts.

maya: attaching the short CSV excerpt:
```
ts,cohort,prefix_hits,prefix_lookups,evictions
10:00,A,410,1000,12
10:01,A,398,980,18
10:02,B,5,520,9
```

observability-bot: Dashboard snapshot: https://redwood.internal/obs/dashboards/prefix-cache?pool=8x&from=2026-11-03T10:00Z

li: quick mitigation idea: favor affinity grouping inside the batcher — prefer to pack same-prefix requests together and set a max_cross_prefix_fraction=0.25 so a batch can't be >25% mixed. That should keep warm prefixes concentrated and reduce KV churn.

josh: SGTM. Also we should try lowering batch_window back to 10ms in canary and enable an eviction-smoothing param (kv.eviction_decay=0.6) to avoid rapid churn.

maya: I'll spin a canary with: batch_window=10ms, affinity_grouping=on, kv.eviction_decay=0.6, kernel=fused-attn-v2 rollback if no improvement in 15m.

li: FYI: I instrumented kernel selection trace — the new fused-attn path increases per-request mem-alloc jitter which slightly delays KV prefetch in ~8% of cases. That plus mixed batches explains the hit-rate gap. I'll open a small PR to add an early-prefetch hook in fused-attn.

josh: nice. also, we should add a short-lived perf test that injects a synthetic cold cohort to ensure we don't regress again. Could be part of the rollout checklist.

maya: working on canary now, will post numbers in 10m. thanks all :thumbsup:

infra-bot: Canary deployment started: rollout/continuous-batcher-v3-canary -> pool:8x (10% traffic). Job id: infra/5678

maya: canary update: after 12 minutes prefix_hit_rate for cohort A improved to 63% with affinity_grouping on and window=10ms. p95 latency at 40ms. Looks promising.

josh: great. let's keep canary 30m then promote. Also li's prefetch hook PR would be good to include before full rollout.

li: opening PR with tests and microbenchmark. ETA 2hrs.

maya: cool — marking this thread for follow-up post-promote to capture post-rollout metrics and any residual tail effects.

josh: noted. thanks everyone.
